JUDGMENT This petition is filed by the L.R's of one deceased Sri Somashekariah.B under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.45,00,000/- in respect of his death in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 09.05.2023 at about 4.30 pm Somashekaraiah.B was walking on the platform of BMTC bus stop, Yelahanka, 4th Phase Yelahanka Upanagar, Bengaluru at that time one MBTC Electric Bus bearing No.KA- 51-AH-2558 driven by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner dashed against Somashekaraiah, due to which he sustained grievous injury and his heart came out of the body and he died on the spot itself.
Later his body was brought to government hospital, Yelahanka and post mortem was conducted and handed over the dead body to the petitioners.

Petitioners have shifted the dead body to Turvekere Taluk, Tumkur Dist and performed funeral and obsequies by spending Rs.3,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
transportation of dead body and other incidental expenses.

3. Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy having good health and was working as Conductor in BMTC and was drawing salary of Rs.46,647.74/- per month and he was contributing his entire income to the family.
Petitioners were solely dependents on him.
Petitioner no.1 being wife of deceased has lost caretaker husband and petitioner no 2 to 4 are daughters of deceased have lost care taker father.
The Yelahanka Traffic police have registered Crime No.177/2023 against the said driver for the offence P/U/S 279 and 304(a) of IPC.
The accident is occurred due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus.

The 1 st respondent is the R.C. owner and 2nd respondent being the hirer and 3 rd respondent is insurance company of aforesaid bus and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
On all these grounds petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.45,00,000/- with costs and interest in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 is served.
He remained absent on the date of hearing and placed exparte.
Respondent no.2 filed written statement and denied the petition averments and contended that the 1st respondent is the R.C owner and custodian of the offending vehicle.
This respondent is the hirer of the bus for rent to ply on the routes belongs to this respondent BMTC and BMTC is paying rent to 1st respondent.
Except this 2nd respondent has no control over the bus including the driver.
The 1 st respondent itself holds entire control over the offending bus.
That the bus is insured by the 1st respondent company with 3rd respondent insurance company and the policy was valid as on the date of accident.
The driver of the bus had valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
Therefore liability if any is of the 1 st and 3rd respondents and not of this respondent.
He denied the manner of accident.
That a false case is registered against the driver of the bus in collusion with police.
On all these grounds 2 nd respondent prayed to dismiss the claim petition against him.

Kala.B vs Switch Moblility on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69955117/
2 5.

Respondent no.3 insurance company has filed written statement and denied the petition averments and contended the policy 7170031220300009180 was not pertaining to BMTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA-51-AH-2558 and that on the date of accident i.e., 09.05.2023 the said bus was not having valid insurance policy.
Hence the entire claim petition deserves to be dismissed against the 3rd respondent.

Further the owner of the vehicle is duty bound to submit all vehicular documents as mandated under Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act, and the concerned police have not complied the provisions of Sec.158(6)of M.V.ACT.
That petitioner colluding with the owner of the bus and police, to get compensation by this respondent have falsely implicated this bus.
That the alleged accident took place due to the negligence on part of the deceased.

That claim petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties as the driver of BMTC bus is not made as party to the proceeding who is also necessary party for the adjudication of the above claim.

That the driver of BMTC bus was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding such driving license and further not satisfied the requirements of Rule 3 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
Thereby owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions fo the policy.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
That the said bus was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident and has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The age, occupation, income and permanent dependency alleged by the petitioners all are denied.
Manner of accident alleged by the petitioners is denied.
On all these grounds it prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, this court has framed following;
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that, on 09.05.2023 one Somashekaraiah.B was walking on platform of BMTC bus stop, Yelahanka 4th Phase, Yelahanka Upanagara, Bengaluru and at that time, one BMTC Electric Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AH-2558 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner in high speed dashed against the said Somashekaraiah.B and caused accident and he sustained injuries and died on the spot as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age, occupation, income of deceased and their permanent dependency on him?
3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves that 1st respondent is the owner of the bus and 2 nd respondent is paying rent to 1st respondent to ply on the routes as alleged?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5. What Order or Award?
ADDITIONAL ISSUE 6. Whether petitioner proves that respondent no.3 has issued policy of insurance in respect of vehicle No.KA-51-AH-2558 in the above case?

3 7.
To prove the case of the petitioners, 1 st petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through her Ex.P.1 to P.26 documents are marked.
One Prakash Hadpad, conductor of BMTC bus is examined as P.W.2.
One eye witness by name Ningappa is examined as P.W.3.
No documents is marked on behalf of P.W.2 and 3.
They are fully cross examined.
Respondents have not led any evidence on their behalf.
8. Heard learned counsel for both sides.
During the course of arguments, 2nd respondent has filed memo with copy of relevant portion of service agreement between respondent no.1 and 2 in respect of issue no.3 in the present case.
Perused the records.

9. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.4 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Addl
. Issue No.6 :

To prove the accidental injuries sustained by her husband and his consequential death she has produced FIR registered by Yelahanka Traffic police on the information given by Nandini K.S who is daughter of deceased.
It is mentioned in the first information that, her father sustained injury due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus bearing No.KA-51-AH-2558 on the platform of the Yelahanka bus stand.
On the basis of that informant Yelahanka police registered Crime No.177/2023 against the driver of the said bus .
After investigation they filed charge sheet against one Mounish Talavar who is driver of aforesaid bus.

It is mentioned in the charge sheet that while the said driver was trying to board the passengers he lost control over the bus and hit the conductor V.Somashekaraiah who was walking on the platform and the bus went again and hit the bus stand wall.
It is also mentioned in the charge sheet that inner parts of body of the Somashekaraiah came out and he died on the spot.
Further, due to breakage of the wall Rs. One Lakh damage is also caused to the bus stand.
11. In the spot panchanama, the place of accident is shown on the platform.
One Ningappa who is eye witness mentioned about the negligence of the said bus driver in his statement before the police.
In the spot panchanama it can be seen that there was sufficient place to stop the bus as it was bus stand.
The IMV report is not produced.
As per the post mortem report death is due to poly trauma resulting in severe hemorrhage of the blood leading to hypovolunerick shock causing death.
The post mortem was conducted on 09.05.2023 on the date of accident itself.

Kala.B vs Switch Moblility on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69955117/
4 12.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 there is no suggestion as to accident is not due to rash and negligent driving of the bus driver.
There is only suggestion that accident was caused due to the negligence of the husband of P.W.1 as he entered the platform without observing the bus.
The said suggestion is denied by P.W.1.
To support the case of P.W.1 the same bus conductor is examined as P.W.2.
he stated that, the said bus driver himself is responsible for accident.
He further stated that he himself was injured in the said accident.
He denied material suggestion in cross examination.
The suggestion that deceased was walking in the middle of the platform without observing the bus is pleaded ignorance by this witness.
He stated that, Somashekaraiah was walking on the upper portion of the platform nearby to the place where the buses will be parked.
Further, one eye witness by name Ningappa is examined.
He stated that he is eye witness to the accident and he was in the bus stand at that time.
That bus had to stop in the platform but suddenly it got the speed and bus rushed to the near by kitchen along with the person and the persons body parts scrambled.
According to this witness it is due to driver who had to press the brake but instead he pressed the accelerator due to which accident caused.
He specifically denied there was negligence of the deceased in the accident.
13. To deny these contentions, and to support the claim of the respondents that it was due to the negligence of the deceased he sustained accident, respondents have not led any evidence.
They only cross examined the petitioners side witnesses but could not elicit anything about the negligence of the deceased in the accident.
The entire record shows that deceased was on the platform while the bus had to stop nearby but it did not and hit the person/ deceased who was on the platform.

Therefore, in the opinion of this court on the basis of oral and documentary evidence, petitioners have proved that the driver of bus bearing No.KA-51-AH-2558 was rash and negligent in driving the bus.
Accordingly this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2 :
To prove the age of the deceased petitioners have produced aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P.2 and his conductor licence at Ex.P.4.
They show that he was born on 01.07.1963.
As on the date of accident i.e. 09.05.2023 deceased was aged 59 years.
The age of the deceased is not seriously disputed.
His ID card also proves the same.
Therefore it is considered that he was aged about 59 years at the time of accident.
15. It is stated in the petition that deceased was bus conductor.
Respondents have disputed the same.
But his conductor licence is produced at Ex.P.4 along with his salary certificate at Ex.P.5.
They show that he was bus conductor and his licence was renewed from time to time.
As per salary certificate he was earning gross salary of Rs.34,909/- and net salary of Rs.30,546/-.
Though this income is disputed, no contrary evidence is produced to disbelieve the case of petitioners.
Considering the deducted it is proper to hold that his monthly income is Rs.30,546/- .
Accordingly his monthly income is considered as Rs.30,546/-.
The person dead is husband of 1st petitioner and father of petitioner no.2 to 4.
It is stated that daughters are married therefore they are not dependents.
As per the settled law on the point, even the major children can file petition seeking compensation not only on the ground of conservative heads but on all heads.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court, all of them will have to be considered as dependents upon him.

Accordingly,
this issue is answered Partly in the Affirmative.

Kala.B vs Switch Moblility on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69955117/
5 16.
ISSUE No.3:
In his written statement 2nd respondent contended that 1st respondent is the owner of the bus and 2 nd respondent is paying rent to 1st respondent to ply on the routes.
To prove the same, 2nd respondent has not lead any evidence.

But during the course of arguments, counsel for 2nd respondent produced one copy of service agreement in which it is mentioned that 1st respondent is the owner of the offending bus and 2nd respondent has allowed him to ply on the routes in which BMTC bus has to travel.
Therefore, though evidence is not led by producing the document the contention of the 2 nd respondent is prove.
That apart, 1st respondent has not disputed his ownership to the bus or permit given to him to ply on the routes as per the BMTC rules in terms of service agreement.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court 2 nd respondent has proved this issue in his favour.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.4:

In view of above reasons, it can be inferred that death of Somashekaraiah is due to the RTA occurred on 09.05.2023 by rash and negligent driving of the Bus bearing No.KA-51-AH-2558 hence petitioners are entitled for compensation from the hands of respondents.
Since the existence of valid insurance policy as on the date of accident is proved, 3rd residing insurance company is liable to pay compensation to petitioners.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under;
(i) Loss of dependency :
As per the Praney Sethi case future prospects of the deceased will have to be added to the monthly income.
In case of salaried persons 15% of the actual salary has to be added to the monthly income to the age group between 50 to 60 years.
Age of the deceased in this case is 59 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, in the present case the monthly income of deceased is Rs.30,546/- + 4,581/- = Rs.35,127/-.
Further deceased being married having 4 dependent 1/4 of his income shall be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Hence, the loss of dependency is calculated as Rs.26,345 X 12 months = Rs.3,16,140/- X 9 multiplier to the age group of 56- 60 years = Rs.28,45,260/-.

As such, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.28,45,260 /-
(ii) Loss of love and affection: Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their husband and father respectively, hence for loss of love and affection compensation of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
(iii) Loss of Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/- and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/- respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.

As such, accident being taken place in the year 2023, under the head of loss of estate Rs.16,500/-, for funeral expenses Rs.16,500/- and for loss of consortium Rs.44,000/- each to petitioner No.1 to 4 is awarded.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:
 Sl. Particulars of Heads Amount in Rs.
 i. Loss of Dependency : 28,45,260 /-
 ii. Loss of love & affection : 50,000/-
 iii. Loss of Consortium to : 1,76,000/-
 petitioner No. 1 to 4,
 ( Rs.44,000/- each)
Kala

6  iv. Loss of estate : 16,500/-
 v. Funeral expenses : 16,500/-
 TOTAL Rs. 31,04,260/-
Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for a compensation of Rs.31,04,260/- Hence, I answer this Issue in "Partly Affirmative".
18. ISSUE NO.5:
In view of above reasons petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.31,04,260/- with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of payment.

Counsel for 3rd respondent contended that the valid insurance policy was mentioned much later to the filing of petition and therefore interest may be ordered from the date when the correct policy is mentioned.
According to him, due to the negligence of petitioners there is delay in mentioning the proper insurance policy and for that 3rd respondent cannot be made to pay interest.
It is necessary to notice that initially insurance policy number was wrongly mentioned by the petitioner in the cause title of the petition.
Subsequently, by filing necessary application correct policy is mentioned.
In the answer to IMV notice owner himself has given incorrect policy number which can be noticed from Ex.P.12 which is answer to IMV notice.
When owner himself has not properly given the insurance policy, petitioners being victims of the accident cannot be blamed.

Later by efforts of the petitioners,
they identified the correct policy number and mentioned the same by filing necessary I.A.
3rd respondent has not even led his evidence to contend that from which date interest should be awarded.
Therefore his contention that interest should be awarded from the date when correct policy number cannot be accepted.
Accordingly, interest shall be awarded from the date of petition.
Petitioner No.1 to 4 being wife and married daughters of the deceased are entitled to the compensation in the apportionment of 40:20:20:20.

In such apportionment 50% amount awarded to petitioner no.1 shall be ordered to be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be ordered to be released in her favour.
The entire compensation awarded to petitioner No.2 to 4 shall be released in their favour without making F.D.
Accordingly, this issue is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
19. ADDITIONAL ISSUE NO.6:
Petitioners by filing necessary application have mentioned the correct policy number in respect of the vehicle involved in the present case.
3 rd respondent not led evidence to contend that he has not issued any policy to the offending vehicle.
Therefore, petitioners have proved this point.
Accordingly this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.5:

In view of the above reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.31,04,260/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment from respondents.

Kala.B vs Switch Moblility on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69955117/
7

In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.3 shall indemnify the insured and hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this tribunal within 2 months from the date of this order.
Out of the total amount with cost and interest awarded, petitioners are entitled to the compensation in the apportionment of 40:20:20:20.

In such apportionment 50% amount awarded to petitioner no.1 shall be ordered to be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be ordered to be released in her favour.
The entire compensation awarded to petitioner No.2 to 4 shall be released in their favour without making F.D.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

The entire compensation awarded to petitioner No.2 to 4 shall be released in their favour without making F.D.
Accordingly this issue is answered in the Affirmative.

ORDER
